mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods meeting the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 for three consecutive months signals labor market strength, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >100,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with PAYEMS increases >100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.3% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by >0.3% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of four consecutive months with INDPRO declines >0.3%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during months when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by >1%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising above 2% per year, the central bank is likely to remain accommodative, supporting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and cost of capital, ultimately producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of six consecutive months with UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns at the 5-day horizon, such that monthly RSAFS growth above 0.5% predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) when RSAFS monthly growth exceeds 0.5%.
